title: Gaussian two-function inequality for continuous functions
statement:
Let $n$ be a natural number, and let $r,s,\rho\in\mathbb R$ satisfy $r>0$, $s>0$, $rs\le 1$, $0\le\rho\le 1$, and $\rho^2\le rs$. Suppose the two coordinate projections of the joint Gaussian law of $(X,\rho X+\sqrt{1-\rho^2}Y)$ each have standard Gaussian product measure as their distribution, where $X,Y$ are independent standard Gaussian vectors in $\mathbb R^n$. For continuous real-valued functions $F,G$ on the torus $(\mathbb R/\mathbb Z)^{\{1,\ldots,n\}\times\{0,1\}}$, one has
\[
\mathbb E\bigl[|F(T(X))|\,|G(T(\rho X+\sqrt{1-\rho^2}Y))|\bigr]
\le \left(\int |F(T(x))|^{1+r}\,d\gamma(x)\right)^{1/(1+r)}
\left(\int |G(T(x))|^{1+s}\,d\gamma(x)\right)^{1/(1+s)},
\]
where $\gamma$ is standard Gaussian product measure and $T(x)$ has coordinate $x_i$ in the first torus block and $\sqrt2x_i$ in the second block, each taken modulo $1$.
hypotheses_covered: The first coordinate projection of the joint Gaussian measure preserves the standard Gaussian product measure
The second coordinate projection of the joint Gaussian measure preserves the standard Gaussian product measure
$F$ and $G$ are continuous real-valued functions on the specified torus
